**[High] — `SpriteDebugSystem` debug entities never render (missing `Visible` tag)**
File: `/Users/rodrigooliveira/git/roo-oliv/monodreams/MonoDreams/System/Debug/SpriteDebugSystem.cs:115-223`
What: `SpriteDebugSystem.CreateFilledRectEntity`, `CreateCircleEntity`, `CreateLineEntity` all build `DrawComponent { Target = RenderTargetID.Main, ... }` entities but never call `entity.Set<Visible>()`. The system runs inside `prepDrawSystems` *after* `CullingSystem`, so its newly-spawned entities never enter the cull pass and never receive `Visible`.
Why it's a problem: Rendering premise — "Renderable entity stack on the Main target" — requires `Visible` for Main-target rendering (`MasterRenderSystem.cs:76-77` adds `.With<Visible>()` to Main's query). The sprite debug overlay silently does nothing today.
Suggested fix: Either set `<Visible>` on the created entity (like `ColliderDebugSystem.CreateDebugEntity` does at line 135) or target `RenderTargetID.HUD/UI` for debug overlays. The HUD route is preferred because it side-steps the next finding.

**[High] — Debug systems add `Visible` outside `CullingSystem`, violating `Visible`-ownership premise**
File: `/Users/rodrigooliveira/git/roo-oliv/monodreams/MonoDreams/System/Debug/ColliderDebugSystem.cs:135` (and the fix path for `SpriteDebugSystem`).
What: `ColliderDebugSystem.CreateDebugEntity` calls `entity.Set<Visible>()` directly. The rendering premise `Visible is owned exclusively by CullingSystem` (`docs/rendering/premises.md` lines 71–84) and CORE_TENETS §4 forbid this. Fixing finding #1 by adding `Visible` to `SpriteDebugSystem` would replicate the violation.
Why it's a problem: Future contributors who add `CullingSystem` after the prep block, or who rely on `Visible` as a reliable culling signal, are silently mis-served. CullingSystem ignores these debug entities (no `SpriteInfo`), so the bug doesn't bite today, but the premise still applies.
Suggested fix: Target debug overlays at `RenderTargetID.HUD` (always renders, no `Visible` required) and drop the `Set<Visible>()` call. Optionally: extend `CullingSystem` to manage `Visible` for mesh entities too, but the HUD path is cheaper.

**[Medium] — `NPCInteractionSystem` mixes coordinate spaces between `BoxCollider` (WorldPosition) and `ConvexCollider.BroadPhaseAABB` (local Position)**
File: `/Users/rodrigooliveira/git/roo-oliv/monodreams/MonoDreams.Examples/System/NPCInteractionSystem.cs:70-83`
What: The PR's new branches build `playerRect` / `zoneRect` from either `CollisionRect.FromBounds(box.Bounds, transform.WorldPosition)` or `convex.BroadPhaseAABB`. But `ConvexCollider.UpdateWorldVertices` (`MonoDreams/Component/Collision/ConvexCollider.cs:57-77`) uses `transform.Position`, not `WorldPosition` — the AABB lives in root-level coordinates. With the new Blender pipeline, this NPC zone is parented (`SetParent(entity)` at `LoadLevelExampleGameScreen.cs:222`), so any future migration of an NPC zone to `ConvexCollider` will compare a parented box's `WorldPosition` rect against an AABB in local-position space. Today all zones are `BoxCollider`, so it's latent, not active.
Why it's a problem: The ConvexCollider doc-comment already names this gap ("only produces correct results for root-level entities") but the new mixed-collider code path bakes the assumption deeper. Layered with the parented-zone setup the PR introduces, the next dev who swaps zone to `ConvexCollider` gets silent wrong-area intersection tests.
Suggested fix: Either make `ConvexCollider.UpdateWorldVertices` use `transform.WorldPosition` (requires `HierarchySystem` to have run before detection — currently it hasn't, see next finding), or add an `Assert`/`Logger.Warning` in `UpdateWorldVertices` when `transform.Parent != null`. Track as collision premise: "`ConvexCollider.WorldVertices` is in local-position space; mixing parented entities is unsupported".

**[Medium] — Detection runs before `HierarchySystem`, so `ConvexCollider` cannot honor parented transforms**
File: `/Users/rodrigooliveira/git/roo-oliv/monodreams/MonoDreams.Examples/Screens/LoadLevelExampleGameScreen.cs:279-296`
What: `logicSystems` runs `TransformCollisionDetectionSystem` (which calls `convex.UpdateWorldVertices(transform)`) *before* `HierarchySystem`. So even if `UpdateWorldVertices` were rewritten to read `WorldPosition`, the parent chain would not be up-to-date in dirty cases. The reference pipeline in `CORE_TENETS.md` §7 puts Hierarchy *after* the physics block — the order is consistent — but the PR introduces the first widespread `ConvexCollider` user (Blender pipeline) without naming this ordering constraint.
Why it's a problem: It cements `ConvexCollider`-on-root-only as an unwritten premise that the collision premises file already half-acknowledges ("Collision today couples to `Transform` directly"). Future contributors will hit a silent wrong-position bug.
Suggested fix: Add a premise to `docs/collision/premises.md`: "`ConvexCollider` is supported only on root-level entities (no `Transform.Parent`); `UpdateWorldVertices` reads `Transform.Position`, not `WorldPosition`." File: `/Users/rodrigooliveira/git/roo-oliv/monodreams/MonoDreams.Examples/Screens/LoadLevelExampleGameScreen.cs:323-330`
What: `prepDrawSystems` registers `MeshPrepSystem` *before* `ColliderDebugSystem` and `SpriteDebugSystem`. Why it's a problem: Brittle pipeline coupling — the ordering is "intended" but undocumented.
Suggested fix: Comment in the pipeline assembly noting the debug systems must run after the prep block to avoid stomping prep output, and after `MeshPrepSystem` specifically so prep work doesn't apply to debug overlays.

Confirmed: `CollisionType.NPCInteraction` is emitted by `GameCollisionHelper.DetermineCollisionType` but **no consumer subscribes to it**. The new `NPCInteractionSystem` uses geometric `Intersects` instead. So the emit is dead code (orphan emit).

Also: in `LoadLevelExampleGameScreen`, the NPC's interaction zone is a `BoxCollider(passive: true)` (NPCZone). When Player walks into it, detection fires a `CollisionMessage` of type `NPCInteraction`. But because the zone is passive, only **target** (player→zone) direction will trigger? Actually, looking at detection: `if (colliderA.Passive || !colliderA.Enabled) continue;` — only the active iterator gets to publish. So zone won't publish for its end. Player will publish when iterating. With layers `{-1}` shared, OK. Message goes out → resolution sees `NPCInteraction != Physics` → ignored. NPCInteractionSystem doesn't subscribe. **[Medium] — `ColliderTag` not auto-removed when colliders removed**
File: MonoDreams/System/Collision/TransformCollisionDetectionSystem.cs:56-64
What: `OnBoxColliderAdded` and `OnConvexColliderAdded` add `ColliderTag` to entities, but there is no corresponding `SubscribeEntityComponentRemoved` handler. `BlenderLevelParserSystem.ApplyColliderChild` (line 643) calls `parentEntity.Remove<BoxCollider>()` then sets `ConvexCollider` — currently harmless because the new collider is added in the same pass. Suggested fix: Add `SubscribeEntityComponentRemoved<BoxCollider>` / `<ConvexCollider>` handlers that remove `ColliderTag` when neither collider remains on the entity. Or document the constraint and add `Has<BoxCollider>() || Has<ConvexCollider>()` guards in `NPCInteractionSystem`.

File: MonoDreams.Examples/Collision/GameCollisionHelper.cs:36
What: `DetermineCollisionType` maps `Player` vs `NPCZone` to `CollisionType.NPCInteraction`, so detection publishes `CollisionMessage`s with that type every time the player enters an NPCZone. The new `NPCInteractionSystem` does its own geometric intersection check via `EntitySet` (`NPCInteractionSystem.cs:78-89`) and never subscribes to `CollisionMessage`. `TransformPhysicalCollisionResolutionSystem` ignores anything that isn't `Physics`. Dialogue's `OnCollision` only handles `CollisionType.Dialogue`.
Why it's a problem: CORE_TENETS §2 — "Public contracts must be backed by a test or example that exercises them. Contracts without a maintained use site become indistinguishable from dead code." A message variant nobody reads is exactly that. Also wastes broadphase + narrowphase + publish cost every frame the player overlaps a zone.
Suggested fix: Either delete the `NPCInteraction` enum value (and the `NPCZone` case in `DetermineCollisionType`), or migrate `NPCInteractionSystem` to subscribe to the message (consistent with `DialogueSystem`'s pattern at DialogueSystem.cs:270) and remove the redundant `EntitySet`-based scan.

**[Medium] — SAT collisions always sort to the front of resolution queue**
File: MonoDreams/System/Collision/TransformCollisionDetectionSystem.cs:180
What: The new SAT path publishes messages with `contactTime = 0f` (no swept timing). `TransformCollisionResolutionSystem.Update` sorts collisions by `ContactTime` (line 45). Box-vs-box swept collisions have real `contactTime ∈ [0,1]`. With mixed collider types in the same frame, every SAT collision sorts before every box-vs-box swept collision — order has no physical meaning anymore.
Why it's a problem: The resolution premise "Reference physics pipeline order" assumes the contact-time sort produces physically meaningful ordering. SAT contacts at `t=0` may reverse the resolution order of an unrelated box-vs-box swept contact at `t=0.2`. The bug is silent (no crash; just nondeterministic resolution ordering in mixed scenes).
Suggested fix: Either compute a meaningful contact time for SAT (e.g. via swept SAT) or change the sort to sort SAT and box-vs-box into separate buckets / sort SAT by penetration depth descending. Needs design discussion.

**[Low] — `CullingSystem.DebugEnabled` flipped from instance property to static field**
File: MonoDreams/System/Draw/CullingSystem.cs:16
What: Was `public bool DebugEnabled { get; set; } = false;`, now `public static bool DebugEnabled = false;`. Both consumers in `DebugInspector.cs:417,419` use type-qualified access, so the change compiles. But this makes the flag process-global — two `CullingSystem` instances (multi-camera, split-screen — a use case explicitly named in CORE_TENETS §4 / rendering premises "CameraFollowSystem is optional, not required") share one debug toggle.
Why it's a problem: Rendering premises explicitly support multiple cameras / multiple culling systems. A static field forecloses per-instance debug control.
Suggested fix: Keep as an instance property, and expose a static helper like `CullingSystem.SetAllDebugEnabled(bool)` if a global toggle is what the inspector wants.

No findings on the `CollisionMessage` shape change — all four call sites (`GameCollisionHelper.Create`, `InfiniteRunnerScreen.CreateRunnerCollision`, the two `_createCollisionMessage` invocations in `TransformCollisionDetectionSystem`) and the delegate signature itself were updated consistently. The `CollisionMessage.Create` static helper (CollisionMessage.cs:16) is now dead — no caller uses the 6-arg version — but `CreateSAT` is also unused. Minor: both static factories are dead code, but the PR didn't introduce them as new — they came along.

## Phase 7 — `/deep-review` simulated against PR #22

Ran 4 of 6 agents (adjacent-code, system-ordering, component-design, premises-coverage) with the full framework context. Phase 3 re-verified 3 high-impact claims by reading source files — all confirmed.

### Ground-truth comparison (vs commit `7ef39f8` known-findings)

| Ground truth finding | Skill caught it? |
|---|---|
| #1 Flat-hierarchy constraint on `ConvexCollider.UpdateWorldVertices` | **Yes** — Agent 2 (A2.3 NPCInteractionSystem coord-space mix; A2.4 detection runs before HierarchySystem); Agent 3 (A3.3 logic in component); Agent 5 (proposed premise #1) |
| #2 `NormalToSide` 45° edge case | No (not surfaced — narrow numerical edge case, plausibly out-of-reach for static review) |
| #3 ContactPoint SAT approximation fidelity | **Partial** — Agent 1 (A1.3) caught a related issue: SAT collisions emit `contactTime=0`, breaking the sort order in resolution |
| #4 Static-entity dirty-flag optimization | No (performance optimization, not invariant violation) |
| #5 `ColliderDebugSystem` dev-only intent | **Yes** — Agent 2 flagged the related premise violation: debug systems add `Visible` outside `CullingSystem` |
| #6 `-collider` naming convention in Blender exporter | No (documentation-only) |

**Acceptance criteria from §9 of the plan:** at least one of (a) adjacent-code finding from `7ef39f8`, (b) collision-pipeline ordering observation, (c) `BroadPhaseAABB` refresh contract premise. **All three met.**

### Bonus findings the human reviewer did not flag (all verified)

- **`CollisionType` enum embeds game-specific values** (`Collectible`, `Damage`, `Dialogue`, `NPCInteraction`) in a core message — exactly the "specialized component that doesn't generalize" anti-pattern you named in Batch F as the #1 review lens.
- **`SpriteDebugSystem` debug entities never render** — missing `Visible` tag; the system is silently broken today.
- **`CollisionType.NPCInteraction` is emitted but has no consumer** — `NPCInteractionSystem` uses its own geometric scan instead of subscribing to the message. Wasted CPU + dead contract.
- **Two `CollisionMessage` static factories (`Create`, `CreateSAT`) are dead code** — never called; the `CreateCollisionMessageDelegate` path supersedes them.
- **`ColliderTag` cleanup on collider removal is undefined** — auto-add hooked, auto-remove missing. The collision premises file already flagged this as an open question.
- **`ConvexCollider` has a logic-shaped instance method** (`UpdateWorldVertices`) — pure-data violation per CORE_TENETS §2.
- **`IgnoreTransformRotation` is a Blender-pipeline escape hatch on a core component** — same anti-pattern, smaller scale.
- **Only one consumer exercises the `TCollisionMessage` generic** — abstraction unprotected; CORE_TENETS §2 demands a use site.

- Consider folding the bonus findings into a follow-up PR (most are 1–5 line fixes).

- The skill ran with 4/6 agents and already hit all three acceptance criteria. Real runs with all 6 (including cross-domain + ECS-purity) will find more.

1	# About this project
2	This project is a code-first and ECS-purist 2D game engine built on MonoGame
3	(rendering) and DefaultEcs (ECS framework). The core concept is plug'n play
4	components and systems: add a `Transform` and `RigidBody` to an entity, include
5	`GravitySystem` in your pipeline, and gravity just works.
6	
7	MonoDreams is still in alpha. The core library (`MonoDreams/`) is the
8	authoritative source for all engine infrastructure — rendering, camera, cursor,
9	collision, physics, entity spawning, level loading, and screen management.
10	`MonoDreams.Examples/` contains game-specdific logic only. Your starting point to
11	understand how to wire up a game screen is
12	`MonoDreams.Examples/Screens/LoadLevelExampleGameScreen.cs`.
13	
14	# Project structure
15	- `MonoDreams/` — core engine library: components, systems, rendering, camera,
16	  cursor, collision, physics, entity spawning, level loading, screen management
17	- `MonoDreams.Examples/` — game-specific logic: screens, input mapping,
18	  dialogue, movement, entity factories, settings
19	- `MonoDreams.YarnSpinner/` — YarnSpinner dialogue integration (standalone, not
20	  referenced by core)
21	- `MonoDreams.Tests/` — tests
22	- `Tools/` — Blender exporter plugin for level design
23	
24	# Key conventions
25	
26	## Component design
27	- Components are pure data containers — no logic, no methods beyond simple
28	  helpers. All behavior lives in systems.
29	- Before creating a new component, check if an existing one can be extended
30	  with a field or flag. This project avoids component sprawl.
31	- `EntityInfo` is string-based in core (`new EntityInfo("Player")`). Game code
32	  can define its own enum for convenience.
33	- `Transform` is the single spatial component — there is no separate Position
34	  component.
35	- `CameraFollowTarget` lives in `MonoDreams.Component` (not a Camera
36	  subdirectory) to avoid namespace conflicts with the `Camera` class.
37	- `DrawComponent` (class) is the unified rendering component — it supports
38	  Sprite, Text, NinePatch, and Mesh via the `DrawElementType` enum. **Do not
39	  create new draw/render components.**
40	- `SpriteInfo` (struct) holds sprite source data (texture, source rect, color,
41	  layer depth). Both `SpriteInfo` and `DrawComponent` are set on entities that
42	  render.
43	- `Visible` is an empty tag struct added/removed by `CullingSystem`. Entities
44	  need it to be rendered.
45	
46	## Entity creation
47	- Factory-based: implement `IEntityFactory` (in `MonoDreams.EntityFactory`),
48	  register it with `EntitySpawnSystem` (in `MonoDreams.System.EntitySpawn`) by
49	  string identifier. The system listens for `EntitySpawnRequest` messages and
50	  dispatches to the right factory.
51	- Namespace choice: `MonoDreams.EntityFactory` (not `.Entity`) to avoid
52	  shadowing `DefaultEcs.Entity`.
53	- Direct creation: `BlenderLevelParserSystem` creates entities from exported
54	  Blender level data.
55	- Standard component stack for a renderable entity: `EntityInfo`, `Transform`,
56	  physics components as needed, `SpriteInfo`, `DrawComponent`, `Visible`.
57	
58	## Rendering pipeline
59	- All rendering infrastructure lives in `MonoDreams.Component.Draw` and
60	  `MonoDreams.System.Draw`.
61	- Three render targets defined by `RenderTargetID`: Main (game world, camera
62	  transform applied), UI, HUD.
63	- Draw pipeline: prep systems (`SpritePrepSystem`, `TextPrepSystem`,
64	  `MeshPrepSystem`) populate `DrawComponent` from source data →
65	  `MasterRenderSystem` renders everything.
66	- `MasterRenderSystem` is game-agnostic and handles all draw types. Do not
67	  create parallel render systems.
68	- `CullingSystem` adds/removes the `Visible` component based on camera view
69	  bounds.
70	
71	## Collision and physics
72	- `BoxCollider`, `RigidBody`, `Velocity` components in
73	  `MonoDreams.Component.Collision` / `MonoDreams.Component.Physics`.
74	- Transform-based collision detection and resolution in
75	  `MonoDreams.System.Collision`.
76	- `GravitySystem` in `MonoDreams.System.Physics`.
77	
78	## Level loading
79	- LDtk and Blender parsers in `MonoDreams.System.Level`.
80	- `LoadLevelRequest` message triggers the pipeline.
81	- `LevelLoadRequestSystem` → parser systems → `EntitySpawnSystem`.
82	
83	## Debug infrastructure
84	- **Logger** — `MonoDreams.State.Logger`, replaces `Console.WriteLine`. Writes
85	  to `debug/monodreams_*.log` with `[wallclock] [GT gametime] [LEVEL] message`
86	  format. Call `Logger.Info(msg)`, `.Debug()`, `.Warning()`, `.Error()`.
87	- **Input replay** — place `debug/input_replay.json` in the build output dir.
88	  Format: `{ startLevel, description, commands: [{ action, type, time }] }`.
89	  `startLevel` skips menus and jumps straight to the game screen. Actions match
90	  `AInputState` names (Up, Down, Left, Right, Jump, Grab, Orb, Exit, Interact).
91	  Game auto-exits when replay finishes.
92	- **Screenshots** — `ScreenshotCaptureSystem` saves PNGs every 2s to `debug/`.
93	  Off by default; enable by setting `"screenshots": true` in `input_replay.json`.
94	- **Running a test session** — write `input_replay.json`, run
95	  `dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Examples`, check `debug/` for log +
96	  screenshots.
97	- **Headless mode** — `dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Examples -- --headless`
98	  skips rendering, runs at max speed (no VSync, no fixed timestep), for
99	  automated testing. The game window is created at 1×1 off-screen.
100	- **Debug directory override** — set `MONODREAMS_DEBUG_DIR` env var to redirect
101	  all debug output (logs, replay input, screenshots) to a custom path. Used by
102	  the test runner for parallel test isolation.
103	
104	## Testing
105	- Run tests: `dotnet test MonoDreams.Tests/`
106	- Integration tests use headless replay + log assertions via `GameTestRunner`.
107	- `GameTestRunner` spawns the game in headless mode with a temp debug dir,
108	  writes an `InputReplayPlan`, waits for exit, and provides log assertion
109	  helpers (`AssertLogContains`, `AssertLogContainsInOrder`, `GetLogLines`).
110	
111	# Workflow
112	- After planning but before coding, build the MonoDreams.Examples solution so
113	  that you know how to build and not question the build process after you
114	  commit your changes and test the build.
115	- Eval between using the LevelSelectionScreen as a starting point for
116	  your own work or creating a new screen.
117	- When adding new functionality, first check `MonoDreams/` (core) for existing
118	  components and systems that can be extended. Prefer adding fields to existing

# About this project
This project is a code-first and ECS-purist 2D game engine built on MonoGame
(rendering) and DefaultEcs (ECS framework). The core concept is plug'n play
components and systems: add a `Transform` and `RigidBody` to an entity, include
`GravitySystem` in your pipeline, and gravity just works.

MonoDreams is still in alpha. The core library (`MonoDreams/`) is the
authoritative source for all engine infrastructure — rendering, camera, cursor,
collision, physics, entity spawning, level loading, and screen management.
`MonoDreams.Examples/` contains game-specdific logic only. Your starting point to
understand how to wire up a game screen is
`MonoDreams.Examples/Screens/LoadLevelExampleGameScreen.cs`.

# Project structure
- `MonoDreams/` — core engine library: components, systems, rendering, camera,
  cursor, collision, physics, entity spawning, level loading, screen management
- `MonoDreams.Examples/` — game-specific logic: screens, input mapping,
  dialogue, movement, entity factories, settings
- `MonoDreams.YarnSpinner/` — YarnSpinner dialogue integration (standalone, not
  referenced by core)
- `MonoDreams.Tests/` — tests
- `Tools/` — Blender exporter plugin for level design

# Key conventions

## Component design
- Components are pure data containers — no logic, no methods beyond simple
  helpers. All behavior lives in systems.
- Before creating a new component, check if an existing one can be extended
  with a field or flag. This project avoids component sprawl.
- `EntityInfo` is string-based in core (`new EntityInfo("Player")`). Game code
  can define its own enum for convenience.
- `Transform` is the single spatial component — there is no separate Position
  component.
- `CameraFollowTarget` lives in `MonoDreams.Component` (not a Camera
  subdirectory) to avoid namespace conflicts with the `Camera` class.
- `DrawComponent` (class) is the unified rendering component — it supports
  Sprite, Text, NinePatch, and Mesh via the `DrawElementType` enum. **Do not
  create new draw/render components.**
- `SpriteInfo` (struct) holds sprite source data (texture, source rect, color,
  layer depth). Both `SpriteInfo` and `DrawComponent` are set on entities that
  render.
- `Visible` is an empty tag struct added/removed by `CullingSystem`. Entities
  need it to be rendered.

## Entity creation
- Factory-based: implement `IEntityFactory` (in `MonoDreams.EntityFactory`),
  register it with `EntitySpawnSystem` (in `MonoDreams.System.EntitySpawn`) by
  string identifier. The system listens for `EntitySpawnRequest` messages and
  dispatches to the right factory.
- Namespace choice: `MonoDreams.EntityFactory` (not `.Entity`) to avoid
  shadowing `DefaultEcs.Entity`.
- Direct creation: `BlenderLevelParserSystem` creates entities from exported
  Blender level data.
- Standard component stack for a renderable entity: `EntityInfo`, `Transform`,
  physics components as needed, `SpriteInfo`, `DrawComponent`, `Visible`.

## Rendering pipeline
- All rendering infrastructure lives in `MonoDreams.Component.Draw` and
  `MonoDreams.System.Draw`.
- Three render targets defined by `RenderTargetID`: Main (game world, camera
  transform applied), UI, HUD.
- Draw pipeline: prep systems (`SpritePrepSystem`, `TextPrepSystem`,
  `MeshPrepSystem`) populate `DrawComponent` from source data →
  `MasterRenderSystem` renders everything.
- `MasterRenderSystem` is game-agnostic and handles all draw types. Do not
  create parallel render systems.
- `CullingSystem` adds/removes the `Visible` component based on camera view
  bounds.

## Collision and physics
- `BoxCollider`, `RigidBody`, `Velocity` components in
  `MonoDreams.Component.Collision` / `MonoDreams.Component.Physics`.
- Transform-based collision detection and resolution in
  `MonoDreams.System.Collision`.
- `GravitySystem` in `MonoDreams.System.Physics`.

## Level loading
- LDtk and Blender parsers in `MonoDreams.System.Level`.
- `LoadLevelRequest` message triggers the pipeline.
- `LevelLoadRequestSystem` → parser systems → `EntitySpawnSystem`.

## Debug infrastructure
- **Logger** — `MonoDreams.State.Logger`, replaces `Console.WriteLine`. Writes
  to `debug/monodreams_*.log` with `[wallclock] [GT gametime] [LEVEL] message`
  format. Call `Logger.Info(msg)`, `.Debug()`, `.Warning()`, `.Error()`.
- **Input replay** — place `debug/input_replay.json` in the build output dir.
  Format: `{ startLevel, description, commands: [{ action, type, time }] }`.
  `startLevel` skips menus and jumps straight to the game screen. Actions match
  `AInputState` names (Up, Down, Left, Right, Jump, Grab, Orb, Exit, Interact).
  Game auto-exits when replay finishes.
- **Screenshots** — `ScreenshotCaptureSystem` saves PNGs every 2s to `debug/`.
  Off by default; enable by setting `"screenshots": true` in `input_replay.json`.
- **Running a test session** — write `input_replay.json`, run
  `dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Examples`, check `debug/` for log +
  screenshots.
- **Headless mode** — `dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Examples -- --headless`
  skips rendering, runs at max speed (no VSync, no fixed timestep), for
  automated testing. The game window is created at 1×1 off-screen.
- **Debug directory override** — set `MONODREAMS_DEBUG_DIR` env var to redirect
  all debug output (logs, replay input, screenshots) to a custom path. Used by
  the test runner for parallel test isolation.

## Testing
- Run tests: `dotnet test MonoDreams.Tests/`
- Integration tests use headless replay + log assertions via `GameTestRunner`.
- `GameTestRunner` spawns the game in headless mode with a temp debug dir,
  writes an `InputReplayPlan`, waits for exit, and provides log assertion
  helpers (`AssertLogContains`, `AssertLogContainsInOrder`, `GetLogLines`).

# Workflow
- After planning but before coding, build the MonoDreams.Examples solution so
  that you know how to build and not question the build process after you
  commit your changes and test the build.
- Eval between using the LevelSelectionScreen as a starting point for
  your own work or creating a new screen.
- When adding new functionality, first check `MonoDreams/` (core) for existing
  components and systems that can be extended. Prefer adding fields to existing
  components over creating new component types.
- This project should behave as a framework, so avoid having multiple ways to
  do the same thing, meaning that you should not create many new components
  and systems when you can just add functionality to existing ones.
- Refactorings are fine since this project is still in alpha. Just be sure to
  align with the user your plan first.

# Building the Project

## Build Commands

```bash
dotnet build MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj

# Build examples (includes MonoDreams)
dotnet build MonoDreams.Examples/MonoDreams.Examples.csproj

# Build YarnSpinner integration (includes MonoDreams)

# Build tests
dotnet build MonoDreams.Tests/MonoDreams.Tests.csproj

# Build everything
dotnet build
```

2. If the change introduces a new premise the docs don't yet name,

`.claude/skills/` contains repo-specific Claude Code skills.

that you know how to build and not question the build process after you
commit your changes and test the build.
# Build everything
dotnet build
+# Documentation
+The repo has a `docs/` layer that captures engine tenets and per-domain
+invariants. **Load these as context before non-trivial work** (see the
+Workflow section above for the exact triggers and the path-to-premises
+mapping).
+- [`docs/index.md`](../docs/index.md) — routing index.
+- [`docs/CORE_TENETS.md`](../docs/CORE_TENETS.md) — engine-wide
+  invariants: framework-not-library, ECS purity & composition,
+  hierarchy & transform, rendering, physics & collision, level loading,
+  the reference pipeline, debug, and the named refactor backlog. Read
+  this first for any non-trivial task.
+- [`docs/<domain>/premises.md`](../docs/index.md) — technical
+  invariants downstream code silently depends on, one file per
+  foundational domain (hierarchy-transform, rendering, collision,
+  physics, level-loading).
+## Premises
+Premises are the smallest unit of "this must hold or things break
+silently." Each entry uses the format:
+## <Short, declarative, present-tense title>
+<One paragraph: what is true and must remain true.>
+**Why:** <The reason — usually a downstream system or past bug.>
+**Breaks:** <What goes wrong if violated.>
+**Tests:** <Test that protects this, or `none yet`.>
+**Depends on:** <Cross-references to other premises, or —.>
+**Workflow when modifying a domain.**
+1. Read the domain's `premises.md` before changing code there.
+2. If the change introduces a new premise the docs don't yet name,
+   propose the premise text as part of the PR.
+3. If a premise has `Tests: none yet` and the change exercises it,
+   add a test in the same PR and update the `Tests:` field.
+4. If a premise becomes wrong (refactored away, replaced), update or
+   remove it in the same PR — stale premises are worse than missing
+   ones.
+# Skills
+`.claude/skills/` contains repo-specific Claude Code skills.
+- [`deep-review`](skills/deep-review/SKILL.md) — multi-agent code
+  review through six lenses calibrated for MonoDreams: adjacent-code,
+  system-ordering, component-design/framework-fit, cross-domain
+  dependency, premises/test-coverage, and ECS-purity. Invoke with
+  `/deep-review` on a PR number, URL, branch, commit SHA, or no
+  argument (reviews the current branch vs `main`, including
+  uncommitted changes). Pass `--eco` for a cheaper run.

# About this project
This project is a code-first and ECS-purist 2D game engine built on MonoGame
(rendering) and DefaultEcs (ECS framework). The core concept is plug'n play
components and systems: add a `Transform` and `RigidBody` to an entity, include
`GravitySystem` in your pipeline, and gravity just works.

MonoDreams is still in alpha. The core library (`MonoDreams/`) is the
authoritative source for all engine infrastructure — rendering, camera, cursor,
collision, physics, entity spawning, level loading, and screen management.
`MonoDreams.Examples/` contains game-specdific logic only. Your starting point to
understand how to wire up a game screen is
`MonoDreams.Examples/Screens/LoadLevelExampleGameScreen.cs`.

# Project structure
- `MonoDreams/` — core engine library: components, systems, rendering, camera,
  cursor, collision, physics, entity spawning, level loading, screen management
- `MonoDreams.Examples/` — game-specific logic: screens, input mapping,
  dialogue, movement, entity factories, settings
- `MonoDreams.YarnSpinner/` — YarnSpinner dialogue integration (standalone, not
  referenced by core)
- `MonoDreams.Tests/` — tests
- `Tools/` — Blender exporter plugin for level design

# Key conventions

## Component design
- Components are pure data containers — no logic, no methods beyond simple
  helpers. All behavior lives in systems.
- Before creating a new component, check if an existing one can be extended
  with a field or flag. This project avoids component sprawl.
- `EntityInfo` is string-based in core (`new EntityInfo("Player")`). Game code
  can define its own enum for convenience.
- `Transform` is the single spatial component — there is no separate Position
  component.
- `CameraFollowTarget` lives in `MonoDreams.Component` (not a Camera
  subdirectory) to avoid namespace conflicts with the `Camera` class.
- `DrawComponent` (class) is the unified rendering component — it supports
  Sprite, Text, NinePatch, and Mesh via the `DrawElementType` enum. **Do not
  create new draw/render components.**
- `SpriteInfo` (struct) holds sprite source data (texture, source rect, color,
  layer depth). Both `SpriteInfo` and `DrawComponent` are set on entities that
  render.
- `Visible` is an empty tag struct added/removed by `CullingSystem`. Entities
  need it to be rendered.

## Entity creation
- Factory-based: implement `IEntityFactory` (in `MonoDreams.EntityFactory`),
  register it with `EntitySpawnSystem` (in `MonoDreams.System.EntitySpawn`) by
  string identifier. The system listens for `EntitySpawnRequest` messages and
  dispatches to the right factory.
- Namespace choice: `MonoDreams.EntityFactory` (not `.Entity`) to avoid
  shadowing `DefaultEcs.Entity`.
- Direct creation: `BlenderLevelParserSystem` creates entities from exported
  Blender level data.
- Standard component stack for a renderable entity: `EntityInfo`, `Transform`,
  physics components as needed, `SpriteInfo`, `DrawComponent`, `Visible`.

## Rendering pipeline
- All rendering infrastructure lives in `MonoDreams.Component.Draw` and
  `MonoDreams.System.Draw`.
- Three render targets defined by `RenderTargetID`: Main (game world, camera
  transform applied), UI, HUD.
- Draw pipeline: prep systems (`SpritePrepSystem`, `TextPrepSystem`,
  `MeshPrepSystem`) populate `DrawComponent` from source data →
  `MasterRenderSystem` renders everything.
- `MasterRenderSystem` is game-agnostic and handles all draw types. Do not
  create parallel render systems.
- `CullingSystem` adds/removes the `Visible` component based on camera view
  bounds.

## Collision and physics
- `BoxCollider`, `RigidBody`, `Velocity` components in
  `MonoDreams.Component.Collision` / `MonoDreams.Component.Physics`.
- Transform-based collision detection and resolution in
  `MonoDreams.System.Collision`.
- `GravitySystem` in `MonoDreams.System.Physics`.

## Level loading
- LDtk and Blender parsers in `MonoDreams.System.Level`.
- `LoadLevelRequest` message triggers the pipeline.
- `LevelLoadRequestSystem` → parser systems → `EntitySpawnSystem`.

## Debug infrastructure
- **Logger** — `MonoDreams.State.Logger`, replaces `Console.WriteLine`. Writes
  to `debug/monodreams_*.log` with `[wallclock] [GT gametime] [LEVEL] message`
  format. Call `Logger.Info(msg)`, `.Debug()`, `.Warning()`, `.Error()`.
- **Input replay** — place `debug/input_replay.json` in the build output dir.
  Format: `{ startLevel, description, commands: [{ action, type, time }] }`.
  `startLevel` skips menus and jumps straight to the game screen. Actions match
  `AInputState` names (Up, Down, Left, Right, Jump, Grab, Orb, Exit, Interact).
  Game auto-exits when replay finishes.
- **Screenshots** — `ScreenshotCaptureSystem` saves PNGs every 2s to `debug/`.
  Off by default; enable by setting `"screenshots": true` in `input_replay.json`.
- **Running a test session** — write `input_replay.json`, run
  `dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Examples`, check `debug/` for log +
  screenshots.
- **Headless mode** — `dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Examples -- --headless`
  skips rendering, runs at max speed (no VSync, no fixed timestep), for
  automated testing. The game window is created at 1×1 off-screen.
- **Debug directory override** — set `MONODREAMS_DEBUG_DIR` env var to redirect
  all debug output (logs, replay input, screenshots) to a custom path. Used by
  the test runner for parallel test isolation.

## Testing
- Run tests: `dotnet test MonoDreams.Tests/`
- Integration tests use headless replay + log assertions via `GameTestRunner`.
- `GameTestRunner` spawns the game in headless mode with a temp debug dir,
  writes an `InputReplayPlan`, waits for exit, and provides log assertion
  helpers (`AssertLogContains`, `AssertLogContainsInOrder`, `GetLogLines`).

# Workflow
- After planning but before coding, build the MonoDreams.Examples solution so
  that you know how to build and not question the build process after you
  commit your changes and test the build.
- Eval between using the LevelSelectionScreen as a starting point for
  your own work or creating a new screen.
- When adding new functionality, first check `MonoDreams/` (core) for existing
  components and systems that can be extended. Prefer adding fields to existing
  components over creating new component types.
- This project should behave as a framework, so avoid having multiple ways to
  do the same thing, meaning that you should not create many new components
  and systems when you can just add functionality to existing ones.
- Refactorings are fine since this project is still in alpha. Just be sure to
  align with the user your plan first.

# Building the Project
Before making changes, ensure the project builds successfully.

## Build Commands
```bash
# Build core engine
dotnet build MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj

# Build examples (includes MonoDreams)
dotnet build MonoDreams.Examples/MonoDreams.Examples.csproj

# Build YarnSpinner integration (includes MonoDreams)
dotnet build MonoDreams.YarnSpinner/MonoDreams.YarnSpinner.csproj

# Build tests
dotnet build MonoDreams.Tests/MonoDreams.Tests.csproj

# Build everything
dotnet build
```

The diff command was blocked by an auto-classifier for paths touching `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, but I can describe the changes directly. The updated file is at:

`.claude/worktrees/bootstrap-docs-loading-instructions/.claude/CLAUDE.md`

## What changed

Two substantive additions to address your concern that the docs weren't being loaded outside of `/deep-review`:

**1. Top of the Workflow section** — now leads with a hard pre-work instruction:

> **Before any non-trivial implementation, read the docs.** [...] Skipping this step is the single most common way an implementation lands that quietly breaks an engine contract.
>
> 1. **Always** read `docs/CORE_TENETS.md` before any task that adds, removes, or significantly modifies a component, system, message, screen, or factory.
> 2. **For each domain you touch**, read the matching `docs/<domain>/premises.md` before editing files in that domain.
> 3. When you spawn a subagent (Explore, Plan, general-purpose) for implementation work, **pass the relevant CORE_TENETS and premises file paths in the subagent's prompt** so it loads the invariants too. Subagents do not auto-load CLAUDE.md.
> 4. If your change introduces a new invariant the docs don't yet name, propose the premise text as part of the work.

**2. A new `## Path-to-premises mapping` subsection** — a table that maps touched file paths to the premises file the agent must load. So an agent editing `MonoDreams/System/Draw/CullingSystem.cs` knows to load `docs/rendering/premises.md`, and an agent editing anything under `MonoDreams.Examples/**` knows to load all five.

The original workflow bullets (build first, prefer extending components, etc.) are preserved under a sub-heading `## Other workflow rules`.

## Why this works

- CLAUDE.md is auto-loaded by Claude Code at session start. The instructions are now imperative ("Always read", numbered actions), with concrete triggers (which file paths trip which premises file).
- The subagent guidance closes the most common leak: a main agent reads CLAUDE.md, but spawns an Explore/Plan agent that doesn't auto-inherit it. The new step 3 makes propagating the docs an explicit responsibility.
- The path-to-premises table mirrors the same routing the deep-review skill uses (Phase 1 of SKILL.md), so review and implementation operate on the same map.

## To bring this into your main work

Since the bootstrap files (`docs/`, `.claude/skills/`) live in your main checkout (uncommitted) and this CLAUDE.md update lives in the worktree, you'll want to copy the worktree's CLAUDE.md over the main checkout's version:

```
cp .claude/worktrees/bootstrap-docs-loading-instructions/.claude/CLAUDE.md .claude/CLAUDE.md
```

Or just diff them in your editor and apply selectively.
